summary: WebFetch worked for the great majority of this run's targets, so this is a fuller-than-usual result. All 45 supplied verification-batch slugs were attempted; 40 returned real first-party content and are listed in checked_active, while leaseweb.com (near-empty render), vultr.com (403), and nexcess.net (403) could not be read and were left out. Two material status findings came directly from first-party pages read this run: flightcontrol.dev now 301-redirects to ravion.com, whose own page calls Ravion the successor to Flightcontrol built by the same team; and val.town's own homepage displays a 'Sorry, we're closed' banner stating Val Town is shutting down on January 10, 2027. A third, found incidentally during discovery (not part of the supplied batch), is that hathora.dev now 301-redirects entirely to gamefabric.com, a Nitrado-linked game-server platform that does not mention Hathora by name; third-party coverage of an acquisition/handoff was not independently verified and is reported only as unverified context. Discovery searches (WebSearch only, cross-checked against the 276-record inventory to avoid duplicates) surfaced three genuinely new, un-catalogued items, two of which were confirmed by directly fetching their own official pages: Cirrascale (GPU/AI cloud, inference-platform page fetched directly, medium confidence) and Velda (open-source GPU/batch platform, confirmed via its own GitHub repo but the velda.io marketing page itself was not fetched, low confidence). Docker Agentic Platform was found on Docker's own docs site, explicitly labeled experimental, low confidence. All three status alerts are reported for manual review only, per policy, and have not been applied. No pricing was touched; pricing/ is out of scope.

status_alerts.rationale: Fetching https://www.flightcontrol.dev/ directly on 2026-11-16 returned an HTTP 301 redirect to https://www.ravion.com/?from=flightcontrol. Reading that destination page, it calls Ravion 'the successor to Flightcontrol,' built by the same team, says 'nothing changes for existing customers,' and describes a guided, service-by-service migration with both products able to run side by side under one organization. This corroborates the catalog's existing (unverified, confidence=seed) 'transitioning' status with direct first-party evidence; it does not by itself establish a new canonical name/URL, which should go through manual identity review rather than automation.

Fetching https://www.val.town/ directly on 2026-11-16 showed a 'Sorry, we're closed' banner at the top of the page and text stating 'Val Town is shutting down on January 10, 2027,' with a link to a wind-down announcement. This is first-party evidence read directly from the provider's own homepage, not a search snippet.

Found incidentally during discovery, not part of the supplied verification batch. Fetching https://hathora.dev/ directly on 2026-11-16 returned an HTTP 301 redirect to https://gamefabric.com/, a game-server orchestration platform whose page links to Nitrado (via marbis GmbH) but does not mention Hathora by name. The domain-level redirect from hathora.dev is solid first-party evidence that the original site no longer operates independently; the specific narrative (an acquisition by Fireworks AI and a customer handoff to Nitrado) comes only from third-party coverage that was not independently confirmed on any first-party page, so treat that detail as unverified context pending manual review.
